counterfactual_missing_items: no mention of paraproteinemia or serum protein electrophoresis
no mention of non-caseating granulomas to support sarcoidosis
no mention of foreign body material to support foreign body granuloma
response.rationale: R3 is the only candidate fully supported by the specific histologic triad of granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis, Alcian-Blue positive mucin, and multinucleated giant cells, which is characteristic of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma. R4 shares granulomatous and giant-cell features but lacks the decisive necrobiosis and mucin findings. R2 and R1 are nonspecific and do not explain the distinctive mucin and necrobiosis. C1 is a correlated append-only restatement of R3 and adds no independent raw evidence.

rejected.why: Granulomatous inflammation and giant cells are nonspecific; sarcoidosis would not explain central necrobiosis or extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin.
Correlated append-only completion of R3 with no independent raw support; should be discounted as a restatement.
Surgical history is suggestive but histology shows necrobiosis and mucin, not foreign material; foreign body granuloma would not account for Alcian-Blue positive mucin.
Clinical and imaging findings are nonspecific; the specific granulomatous inflammation with necrobiosis and mucin is too characteristic for idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease.
